questions.q: What is the main point of the opening stories of Grace Groner and Richard Fuscone?
options: Investing success depends more on behavior than on knowledge or credentials
Bankers should avoid heavy borrowing and illiquid investments always
Charitable giving is the best possible use of accumulated wealth
A formal education has no value for anyone working in finance
questions.explain: The author says investing is the study of how people behave with money, not of finance.

questions.q: How much did Grace Groner leave to charity?
options: $1 million
$7 million
$20 million
$66 million
questions.explain: She left $7 million to charity after dying in 2010 at age 100.

questions.q: Which economist answered that he most wanted to know the exact role of luck in successful outcomes?
options: Warren Buffett
Scott Adams
Robert Shiller
Richard Fuscone
questions.explain: The author asked economist Robert Shiller, who gave that answer.

questions.q: What does the author say people born in 1970 versus 1950 experienced in their teens and 20s?
options: Stocks rose 10-fold for 1950 births but went nowhere for 1970 births
Stocks rose 10-fold for 1970 births but went nowhere for 1950 births
Stocks fell sharply for both groups, as inflation ate the gains
Stocks tracked inflation closely for both generations of investors
questions.explain: The market went up 10-fold for those born in 1970; for 1950 it went nowhere.

questions.q: What would the author most likely say about someone who tries to earn high returns while avoiding volatility?
options: They are being prudent and will likely succeed in the long run
They are like a car thief trying to take a reward without paying its price
They have found a free lunch that the Money Gods allow
They should simply use more leverage to improve their returns
questions.explain: He compares trades, hedges and leverage to grand theft auto: taking returns without paying the price of volatility.
